validity.researcher_notes: Significant corporate-genealogy finding not reflected anywhere in the sheet: FERC Docket No. CP19-490-000, order issued Dec 2, 2019 (169 FERC P 61,169), approved a joint application by Gulf Crossing Pipeline Company LLC and Gulf South Pipeline Company, LP for (1) Gulf Crossing to abandon-by-transfer its jurisdictional facilities to Gulf South, (2) Gulf South to acquire them via inter-corporate merger and consolidate them into its existing interstate system as a new 'Gulf Crossing Zone' rate zone, effective on or about Jan 1, 2020. The order states explicitly: 'upon Commission authorization of the proposals, Gulf Crossing will no longer exist.' This is NOT a physical decommissioning — the order's own language ('greater operational efficiency,' 'single contract, single nomination, single invoice,' maintaining existing max/min rates in the new zone) makes clear the pipe keeps running exactly as before, just under Gulf South's corporate/tariff umbrella; a later independent tertiary source (offshore-technology.com/GlobalData pipeline database, live URL, checked 2026-09) already lists the pipeline's operator as 'Gulf South Pipeline' rather than Gulf Crossing, corroborating that the post-2020 operating entity is Gulf South. GEM's Owner1='Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' 100% remains true at the ultimate-parent level (Boardwalk owns Gulf South, which now owns the former Gulf Crossing facilities), so I am not flagging it as wrong, but the row's ResearcherNotes/Owner attribution should record that 'Gulf Crossing Pipeline Company LLC' is a defunct entity since ~Jan 2020 and the direct operator of record is Gulf South Pipeline Company, LP — otherwise a future researcher citing a post-2020 Gulf Crossing Pipeline Co LLC filing will be citing a company that no longer exists. validity.researcher_notes: SegmentCost [ref]: I could not find any source stating a $121,000,000 cost for the Gulf Crossing Pipeline, and every capital-cost figure I did find for this project is roughly 10-15x higher. Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' FY2006 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2007), announcing the project, put the *combined* cost of Gulf Crossing plus its associated Gulf South/Fayetteville-Greenville expansions at 'approximately $3.3 billion' for 2007-2009. The FY2008 10-K (filed 2009) itemizes Gulf Crossing separately in its capital-projects table: 'Gulf Crossing Project -- Estimated Total Cost $1,800 [million] -- Cash Invested through December 31, 2008 $1,403.5 [million].' That is consistent with the physical scope (approximately 357 miles of new 42-inch interstate transmission pipeline plus compression, a very large-diameter, long-haul project) -- $121 million would imply roughly $340,000 per mile of 42-inch pipe including compression, which is implausibly low for a 2007-2009-vintage 42-inch interstate line (steel/labor costs were unusually high in that period, which the 10-Ks themselves flag as a cost driver). I searched SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Gulf Crossing' plus '121' / '121,000,000' / '$121 million' and reviewed the FY2006, FY2007, FY2008, and FY2009 Boardwalk 10-Ks directly (all fetched and grepped) -- none contains a $121 million figure tied to Gulf Crossing; the closest analogous number is Boardwalk's Southeast Expansion project (a different, smaller project) at $775 million estimated cost, still far above $121 million. I also checked whether $121 million could be a partial transaction value (e.g., proceeds from Boardwalk's disclosed but apparently unconsummated plan to sell a 49% interest in Gulf Crossing to a third party) -- the 10-Ks mention that structure only in the context of the $3.3 billion aggregate figure and never state a dollar value for the 49% stake itself. WebSearch quota was exhausted for this session (both at the start and again on a later retry) so I could not run open web searches for a possible EIA/trade-press citation of $121 million; everything above came from direct API/document fetches (Federal Register API, SEC EDGAR full-text search, and the four Boardwalk 10-Ks fetched by URL). Given the sheet's own likely source population (other Boardwalk-family pipelines in this cohort, e.g. Tiger and Corpus Christi/Cheniere, show similar single-figure SegmentCost fields that sometimes don't match audited totals), this reads as a probable data-entry or unit/scope error on the sheet -- flagging for Update rather than changing the value or fabricating a citation for it.
